purpose: Evidence graph for disaster resilience across power, mobility, fuel, communications, water, medical continuity, schools, emergency support, public safety, and surveillance. The graph distinguishes confirmed events from causal inference and unverified subsystem uptime.

status_legend.confirmed: Supported directly by a primary or official record.
status_legend.reported: Supported by credible reporting but underlying primary documentation is still sought.
status_legend.confirmed_event_cause_unestablished: The event is documented, but its relationship to the August storm/outage has not been established.
status_legend.vendor_capability: A technical capability described by a vendor; not deployment-specific performance evidence.
status_legend.not_established: The available evidence does not establish the claim.
status_legend.investigate: A comparison or operational question requiring additional records, telemetry, or field evidence.

claims.claim: The August 11, 2026 severe storm caused widespread power outages and infrastructure disruption in Gary.
claims.source: City of Gary storm recovery update, 2026-08-18
claims.next_evidence_needed: NIPSCO feeder, circuit, substation, outage, and restoration data for Gary.

claims.claim: A very large share of Gary customers remained without power more than a week after the storm.
claims.source: Chicago Sun-Times / CBS / Free Press Indiana reporting, August 2026
claims.next_evidence_needed: Time-stamped Gary outage counts plus feeder/circuit restoration records.

claims.claim: Large swaths of Gary were without working traffic signals during the prolonged outage.
claims.next_evidence_needed: Intersection-level signal outage and restoration logs from Gary/INDOT.

claims.claim: By August 18 Gary had assessed 2,097 damage sites and assistance requests, with more than 80% involving fallen trees and blocked roads; 75% of reported blocked roads had reopened.
claims.next_evidence_needed: GIS/timestamped road closure and reopening data by neighborhood.

claims.claim: At least one Gary gas station had nonfunctioning pumps during the outage, while a generator kept part of the business operating and required fuel obtained elsewhere.
claims.next_evidence_needed: Survey/records of gas-station pump operation, generator use, fuel deliveries, and emergency-fleet fuel availability.

claims.claim: The prolonged outage limited residents' ability to store food and manage medications and electrically powered medical devices.
claims.next_evidence_needed: Aggregate emergency-request, medical-device support, spoilage, and displacement data.

claims.claim: Gary established an oxygen-cylinder refill operation for home-use patients affected by the August 11 storms/outages.
claims.source: City of Gary Storm Recovery & Support
claims.next_evidence_needed: Usage totals, operating duration, demand, and referral/transport data.

claims.claim: The Gary YWCA operated as a 24/7 shelter and charging location during recovery.
claims.source: City of Gary Storm Recovery & Support
claims.next_evidence_needed: Facility power source, generator/UPS configuration, capacity, usage, and accessibility records.

claims.claim: AT&T/ITDRC and Verizon deployed charging and connectivity resources in Gary during storm recovery.
claims.source: City of Gary and AT&T disaster updates, August 2026
claims.next_evidence_needed: Carrier outage/degradation records and deployment mission logs.

claims.claim: FirstNet deployed a satellite truck to the NIPSCO facility in Gary to support utility recovery efforts.
claims.limitation: The deployment does not by itself establish a complete outage of existing communications; it may have supplied redundancy, capacity, or replacement service.
claims.next_evidence_needed: FirstNet/NIPSCO deployment rationale, duration, network status, and field-communications logs.

claims.claim: Gary Community School Corporation schools remained closed on August 19 because of ongoing storm-related issues.
claims.next_evidence_needed: District facility outage, closure, reopening, transport, food-service, and communications records.

claims.claim: Indiana American Water issued Gary emergency main-break/boil-advisory notices during the recovery period on August 18, August 20, and August 26, with possible service interruption or low pressure.
claims.limitation: The alerts do not attribute the main breaks to the August 11 storm or electric outage.
claims.next_evidence_needed: Main-break work orders, pressure-zone records, pump-power logs, engineering notes, and maintenance history.

claims.claim: Gary wastewater treatment or pumping experienced storm-related failure, overflow, bypass, or emergency generator operation.
claims.next_evidence_needed: Gary Sanitary District SCADA alarms, plant/pump power logs, generator/fuel logs, overflow/bypass reports, and emergency work orders.

claims.claim: Methodist Hospitals Northlake experienced loss of power or clinical-service interruption during the August storm/outage.
claims.next_evidence_needed: Emergency-power transfer logs, generator/fuel records, incident command records, ED/diversion status, cancellations, and aggregate transfer data.

claims.claim: Gary 911, CAD, dispatch, police radio, or fire communications failed or degraded during the August event.
claims.next_evidence_needed: 911/CAD uptime, radio-system alarms, dispatch continuity, failover, backup-power, and after-action records.

claims.claim: Gary fixed-route transit or paratransit experienced storm-related suspension, missed trips, dispatch failure, or fuel constraints.
claims.next_evidence_needed: GPTC service alerts, dispatch logs, missed trips, route detours, paratransit continuity, garage power, and fuel records.

claims.claim: Gary's RTCC uses surveillance cameras and fixed/mobile license-plate recognition integrated with other public-safety systems.
claims.source: Gary Police Department Real-Time Crime Center

claims.claim: Gary Police Department had an extensive array of Flock cameras by July 2024.
claims.source: Lake County Board of Commissioners minutes, 2024-07-17

claims.claim: Flock describes camera deployments that can use solar/battery power and cellular connectivity.
claims.limitation: This is not evidence of Gary-specific configuration or uptime.

claims.claim: Gary's Flock cameras or RTCC remained operational during the August 2026 power outage.
claims.next_evidence_needed: Device-health telemetry, RTCC logs, power/UPS/generator logs, maintenance records, and carrier-network data.

claims.claim: A valid Gary resilience analysis must compare dependencies, backup power, alternate communications, fuel, physical access, observed outage, restoration time, and evidence quality across resident-facing and government/utility systems.
claims.reporting_question: Which systems were engineered for continuity, which failed, how did failures cascade, and what public values governed resilience investments?
